boardEligibilityNotice: Emory states PET/CT fellowship applicants must have completed a nuclear medicine or radiology residency and be ABNM or ABR board eligible/certified, plus be eligible for unrestricted Georgia licensure. boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course does not establish ABR eligibility. Requirements can change; verify directly with ABR. No examination outcome is predicted or guaranteed.

ABMGG Clinical Biochemical Genetics specialty certification examination (distinct from Medical Biochemical Genetics subspecialty examination; shared Medical/Clinical Biochemical Genetics content blueprint)
boardStatus: A separate ABMGG Clinical Biochemical Genetics specialty examination exists; ABMGG also has a distinct Medical Biochemical Genetics subspecialty examination, and the board publishes a shared Medical/Clinical Biochemical Genetics content blueprint. As of 2026-10-07, the next listed Clinical/Medical Biochemical Genetics exam cycle is 2027; those exams are offered in odd-numbered years. ABMGG requires passing the General exam plus a specialty exam for diplomate status. Hopkins says successful program completion makes trainees eligible to sit, but individual credential/degree requirements remain board-controlled; Hopkins misspells ABMGG as AMBGG. This independent course grants no eligibility.
boardEligibilityNotice: ABMGG states an MD, DO, or qualifying PhD is required for Clinical Biochemical Genetics; completion of accredited training is necessary but individual eligibility depends on board review. A separate and distinct Medical Biochemical Genetics physician subspecialty requires one accredited year after Clinical Genetics and Genomics residency. This is not the same fellowship. Do not infer combined-program status or eligibility from this independent curriculum.

ABMGG includes MFM/Medical Genetics among dual-board-approved combined training options. The exact current programme-specific ACGME accreditation status was not independently confirmed in the public ACGME program finder; Hopkins requires prior ACGME-accredited OB/GYN and describes its broader clinical genetics training programmes as ACGME-accredited. Generic directory “ACGME Accredited or Equivalent” wording is not treated as proof of this particular combined track’s current status. ABOG and ABMGG eligibility/credentialing are board decisions, not guaranteed by this independent course.
boardEligibilityNotice: Only the named institutional programme and each board determine training credit and eligibility. Hopkins states completed ACGME-accredited OB/GYN residency as prerequisite.
